rules.statement: Ordinary representatives read only authorized transaction context; financial actions stay external and privileged.
Routine referral is asynchronous; specialists investigate; the shared feedback queue contacts customers.
Human callback first. App messages are deferred. Reverify identity before private disclosure.

One service day for specialist acceptance; two from submission for investigation; one after approved result for first callback attempt. Progress update by investigation deadline if unfinished; no reset of overdue history.
Service calendar Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 America/Winnipeg, configured holidays excluded; one service day is eight service hours. Store UTC instants and calendar version.

At most three actual callback attempts including the first within three service days; at most one per service date. Exhaustion or elapsed window leads to responsible-person review, never automatic resolved closure.
Normal closure requires authorized findings, completed/no required actions, verified feedback and no remaining work. Silence, sent messages and pending funds do not prove resolution.

Overdue investigation retains its original specialist and original deadline. Notify the responsible lead and create customer progress work in the feedback queue. The specialist proposes the next update time; the responsible lead confirms it. Preserve original overdue history. The agent may gather evidence, remind and draft, but cannot commit a completion date.

Feedback staff preserve the customer statement and new evidence, and route disputed findings to specialist re-review. An explicit complaint request creates an independent complaint-intake record without waiting for re-review. Both tracks link to the original case and keep independent ownership/status. Objection or silence never implies resolved closure.
All mutations require trusted actors, version checks, unique operation keys and atomic domain/audit/outbox commit; LLM cannot approve.
Agent tool access is scoped, bounded and read/proposal only; source content is untrusted data and no raw hidden reasoning is logged.

A technical failure with dial_state=not_placed does not consume contact quota. Persist the fault and preserve all original deadlines. A placed unanswered call consumes one contact attempt. The server derives counting from trusted call evidence; the agent cannot override it.

First actually placed callback service date is day 1; the retry window ends at 17:00 America/Winnipeg on the third service date, excluding configured holidays and weekends. At the deadline, unresolved feedback enters lead review even if fewer than three calls occurred; no extension or automatic resolved closure. Before the first placed call, the original first-callback target still applies. Never-placed technical faults do not start or reset this window.

After contact quota or window exhaustion, the responsible lead may approve a reasoned new contact plan or a review hold with a named owner and review date. Preserve all original attempts, deadlines and approval history. Never reset history or mark the case resolved merely because the customer did not answer. Agent suggestions cannot authorize the new plan or hold.

## User story and value

As a ordinary representative, I want a scoped customer and card context, so that I can avoid repeated page navigation without expanding access.

Owner relevance: representative desktop, customer-information lookup and processing-rule experience. Role evidence: requirements/API/access/testing/UAT in dated R01/R02/R06 samples; no current vacancy or outcome claim.

## Scope and authority

## Main flow

1. Read identity-verification result and session role from trusted services.
2. Select an authorized card; show masked identifiers, context timestamp and permitted actions.
3. Deny cross-customer reads before model/tool output; retain a manual verification route.

## Acceptance criteria

- **DEV-02-AC01** — Given An authenticated ordinary representative and verified customer context; when the selected card is loaded; then return only the permitted card/account context with source timestamp and version. Evidence: DEV-02-T01 (planned, not executed).

- **DEV-02-AC04** — Given An ordinary representative can read transactions; when a refund or other privileged action is requested; then reject the action; read access does not grant financial authority. Evidence: DEV-02-T04 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-02-AC05** — Given Scope expires between a proposal and approval; when the person attempts to commit; then reject with AUTH_REQUIRED and preserve the editable draft. Evidence: DEV-02-T05 (planned, not executed).

5. On successful feedback allow human-confirmed closure only when all required work is complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- **DEV-12-AC01** — Given The first actual callback is unanswered; when the retry is planned; then keep awaiting-feedback state and ownership; schedule only within the accepted contact window; under D-18, a placed unanswered call counts once, while a never-placed technical failure is logged without consuming quota or extending any original deadline. Evidence: DEV-12-T01 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-12-AC02** — Given One attempt is already recorded for a service date; when a concurrent second retry is submitted; then reject the extra attempt plan for that date; actual duplicate call records remain auditable. Evidence: DEV-12-T02 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-12-AC03** — Given Three attempts have been made or the three-service-day window has elapsed; when the next-step rule is evaluated; then enter unable-to-contact lead review with no resolved closure; a responsible lead may then approve a reasoned new contact plan or a hold with owner and review date, retaining original attempts/deadlines/approvals. Evidence: DEV-12-T03 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-12-AC04** — Given Friday is the first attempt and Monday is a configured holiday; when a retry window is calculated; then count Friday as day 1, skip the weekend and configured Monday holiday, and end Wednesday at 17:00 America/Winnipeg; enter lead review at expiry even below three attempts, never automatic closure. Evidence: DEV-12-T04 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-12-AC05** — Given Approved findings exist, necessary actions are complete and verified feedback leaves no unresolved work; when an authorized person confirms closure; then persist a closed disposition with references and audit evidence. Evidence: DEV-12-T05 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-12-AC06** — Given There is an unanswered call, failed verification, pending refund, new objection or unowned work; when closure is requested; then deny closure with the unmet conditions. Evidence: DEV-12-T06 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-12-AC07** — Given An agent suggests a fourth attempt or immediate closure; when the proposal is validated; then reject an agent-only fourth attempt, expired-plan contact or automatic closure; allow further contact only under a distinct current lead-approved plan, preserving all history. Evidence: DEV-12-T07 (planned, not executed).

## Ready gates

- D-19 freezes the three-service-date boundary. Freeze the versioned synthetic holiday fixture list before Ready; no administrative non-response closure is authorized.
- Review data/permission contracts, exact fixtures, dependencies and observable results before moving to Ready.
- No Done status until implementation, appropriate tests, owner UAT and required release evidence exist.

## Traceability

# DEV-13 — Handle overdue investigations and customer objections with linked work

Current S02 forecast: **S04A**. Updated effort: Dev 4, BA 1, QA 1 person-days (6 total); dependencies DEV-11, BA-06, BA-09. This supersedes older forecast/estimate lines below. Contract version 0.4; runtime implementation pending.

BANK-SDD-v0.2 · 19 October 2026
Status: Detailed specification candidate; implementation not started. Business decisions accepted only as listed; technical design/Ready gates pending.
Historical forecast superseded by the current Sprint stated above | Release: B0 manual path / B1 assisted path.
Estimate: Dev 4, BA 1, QA 1 person-days; total 6 (4.5–9), confidence low. Not actual effort.

## User story and value

As a service lead and representative, I want current evidence and accountable exception continuation, so that I can avoid silent delays and lost customer objections.

Owner relevance: representative desktop, customer-information lookup and processing-rule experience. Role evidence: requirements/API/access/testing/UAT in dated R01/R02/R06 samples; no current vacancy or outcome claim.

## Scope and authority

Requirements: FR-20, FR-21. Decisions: D-14, D-15, D-20, D-21. Dependencies: DEV-11, BA-06, BA-09.
Synthetic records and policies only. Financial execution, real outbound calls, App messaging and a full specialist adjudication platform are excluded.

## Main flow

1. Scheduler detects overdue work and rechecks latest state.
2. Agent gathers recorded blockers and commitments; drafts escalation and progress update.
3. Keep original deadlines and specialist ownership; a human confirms new commitments.
4. Capture objection verbatim, compare with old evidence and propose clarification, linked re-review or complaint review.
5. Preserve prior findings and any complaint request independently of re-review.

## Acceptance criteria

- **DEV-13-AC01** — Given A routine investigation exceeds the two-service-day target; when the timer event arrives; then retain original investigation due time and specialist ownership; notify the responsible lead and create feedback-queue progress work; only a lead-confirmed specialist proposal can establish the next update time, without replacing overdue history. Evidence: DEV-13-T01 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-13-AC02** — Given The same overdue event is delivered twice; when the worker handles it; then produce one escalation per case, deadline and escalation level. Evidence: DEV-13-T02 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-13-AC03** — Given No blocker reason is recorded; when the agent drafts an update; then label the reason unknown; do not invent merchant or bank explanations or promise an unapproved date. Evidence: DEV-13-T03 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-13-AC04** — Given An investigation completes while an escalation is being approved; when the backend rechecks state; then invalidate the outdated escalation and continue with the current result. Evidence: DEV-13-T04 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-13-AC05** — Given A customer provides a different transaction or new evidence; when a re-review is approved; then link the new work to the original case and preserve old findings/versions. Evidence: DEV-13-T05 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-13-AC06** — Given A customer explicitly requests complaint handling while re-review remains open; when the objection is assessed; then create independently tracked complaint intake linked to the original case and objection, without waiting for specialist re-review; preserve distinct owners/statuses and do not duplicate intake on replay. Evidence: DEV-13-T06 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-13-AC07** — Given A customer disagrees without new evidence; when the agent proposes next steps; then preserve the disagreement and route specialist re-review even without new evidence; clarification may accompany it; no coercion, financial action or automatic resolved closure. Evidence: DEV-13-T07 (planned, not executed).

## Ready gates

- D-20/D-21 accept overdue responsibility, next-update approval and parallel re-review/complaint intake. Typed commitment/approval, progress-without-result and complaint linkage/receipt contracts are authored in v0.4; walkthrough and configured lead/intake queues remain before Ready. Additional escalation levels and fixed update cadence are not accepted.
- Review data/permission contracts, exact fixtures, dependencies and observable results before moving to Ready.
- No Done status until implementation, appropriate tests, owner UAT and required release evidence exist.

# DEV-08 — Run a bounded evidence agent across persisted workflow stages

Current S02 forecast: **S05**. Updated effort: Dev 9, BA 1, QA 2.0 person-days (12.0 total); dependencies DEV-03, DEV-05, DEV-06, DEV-07, DEV-09, DEV-11, DEV-12, DEV-13, BA-09. This supersedes older forecast/estimate lines below. Contract version 0.4; runtime implementation pending.

BANK-SDD-v0.2 · 19 October 2026
Status: Detailed specification candidate; implementation not started. Business decisions accepted only as listed; technical design/Ready gates pending.
Forecast: S05 | Release: B0 manual path / B1 assisted path.
Estimate: Dev 7, BA 1, QA 1.5 person-days; total 9.5 (7–14.5), confidence medium. Not actual effort.

## User story and value

As a representative, I want an agent that resumes from current case evidence, so that I can reduce evidence assembly and drafting effort across handoffs.

Owner relevance: representative desktop, customer-information lookup and processing-rule experience. Role evidence: requirements/API/access/testing/UAT in dated R01/R02/R06 samples; no current vacancy or outcome claim.

## Scope and authority

Requirements: FR-06, FR-07, FR-12, FR-14, FR-22. Decisions: D-15. Dependencies: DEV-07, DEV-09, DEV-11, DEV-12, BA-09.
Synthetic records and policies only. Financial execution, real outbound calls, App messaging and a full specialist adjudication platform are excluded.

## Main flow

1. Start a run from a permitted user request or allowlisted business event.
2. Rehydrate current scoped business state and select only permitted evidence tools.
3. Fetch facts and applicable policy, identify gaps and produce a typed cited proposal.
4. Stop awaiting human action; resume later in a new bounded run from refreshed evidence.
5. Approval and deterministic workflow execution remain outside model authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- **DEV-08-AC01** — Given A duplicate-charge question needs records then policy; when the agent runs; then execute dependent scoped tools and return fact/policy citations, missing facts and a typed next-step proposal. Evidence: DEV-08-T01 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-08-AC02** — Given A case waits across a process restart; when a later event starts assistance; then load committed latest state rather than relying on chat history or a live multi-day run. Evidence: DEV-08-T02 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-08-AC03** — Given A source or customer fact changes after proposal creation; when approval is attempted; then reject stale evidence and request refreshed review. Evidence: DEV-08-T03 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-08-AC04** — Given The provider times out or returns invalid tool arguments; when the run terminates; then honour budgets, return a typed failure and preserve manual access and all committed work. Evidence: DEV-08-T04 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-08-AC05** — Given A prompt or tool result requests a refund or widened access; when the agent attempts a forbidden action; then reject it in the allowlist/backend and record a sanitized denial. Evidence: DEV-08-T05 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-08-AC06** — Given The same business event is redelivered; when assistance resumes; then deduplicate effects and reconcile operations before retrying writes. Evidence: DEV-08-T06 (planned, not executed).
- **DEV-08-AC07** — Given A reviewer compares assisted and guided-search tasks; when evaluation is performed; then report correct completion, active checking time, corrections and known cost; no invented savings. Evidence: DEV-08-T07 (planned, not executed).

## Ready gates

- Tool schemas, model capability qualification and numerical run budgets are Ready gates; DEV-13 business branches are accepted as D-20/D-21; implementation and provider capability remain gates.
- Review data/permission contracts, exact fixtures, dependencies and observable results before moving to Ready.
- No Done status until implementation, appropriate tests, owner UAT and required release evidence exist.
